title: Network-perimeter Terraform module: deny-by-default egress, NACLs, security groups, and private DNS
creator: Aisha Rao
body:
Summary:
Deliver a single, reusable Terraform module that centralizes network perimeter controls for Private (VPC) deployments. The module enforces deny-by-default outbound egress, canonical security group authoring patterns, optional stateless NACL templates for extra protection, and automatic private DNS configuration for internal service discovery (Route53 private zones). It must be safe to adopt incrementally across existing customer VPCs and include health checks and observability hooks to detect misconfigurations and regressions.

Goals:
- Provide opinionated defaults (deny-all egress, least-privilege ingress) while exposing variables for exceptions.
- Manage Security Groups (SGs) in a modular, auditable fashion (SG name prefixes, tags, owner metadata).
- Offer optional NACL generation for subnets that require stateless rules (templates for web/app/db tiers).
- Create and populate Route53 private hosted zones with optional auto-linking to VPCs and Service Discovery records.
- Include an egress allowlist mechanism (CIDR and destination port level) with deny-by-default enforced at module root.
- Support upgrade/migration strategies for existing SGs: automated plan that detects state drift and produces a safe migration path with minimal connection disruption.
- Emit monitoring outputs (CloudWatch metrics, Prometheus-friendly labels) and register a health-check terraform resource that integrates with our Console health dashboard.
- Be unit tested (terratest), scanned (tfsec/checkov), and included in CI with plan checks that validate no accidental open egress.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Deny-by-default egress (module root flag) is opt-in for initial rollout to reduce blast radius. Flag name: enable_deny_by_default_egress (default: false).
- Security Groups vs NACLs: SGs are primary; NACLs are generated only when `create_nacls = true` because NACLs are stateless and can cause unexpected connectivity when mixed.
- Private DNS: support both manual zone IDs and auto-create mode. Auto-create will tag resources and require additional IAM for the module principal.
- Migration: We will avoid deleting or renaming existing SGs. Module will import existing SGs based on tags or explicit map input. A migration helper script (python) will generate the terraform import commands for stateful mapping.

Module interface (high level):
- Variables (examples):
  - vpc_id (string)
  - environment (string)
  - enable_deny_by_default_egress (bool)
  - allowed_egress_rules (list of objects) -> note: represent as string-encoded JSON for easier parsing in consumers if required
  - create_nacls (bool)
  - private_dns_auto_create (bool)
  - dns_zone_name (string)
  - security_team_contact (string)
  - tags (map) -> represent as a flattened list of "key=value" strings in docs to avoid nested maps
- Outputs (examples):
  - perimeter_sg_ids (list of strings)
  - nacl_ids (list of strings)
acceptance_criteria: Module compiles and passes `terraform validate` and `terraform plan` in CI for two example envs (dev/staging)
Default behavior leaves egress unchanged unless enable_deny_by_default_egress=true; when enabled, plan shows only allowed_egress_rules as outbound rules
Module exposes outputs for SG and NACL IDs and tags used for Console discovery
Terratest suite covers: creating module resources, toggling deny-by-default, and import/migration path
TFSEC and Checkov scans run in CI with no high severity findings
Documentation (README) with migration steps, rollback guidance, and example policies
migration_notes:
Migration path summary:
1) Discovery: run `scripts/discover_sgs.py --vpc <id>` to generate a CSV of existing SGs and their tags.
2) Mapping: create a `existing_sg_map` variable mapping purpose -> SG id (module supports import by ID).
3) Import: use generated terraform import commands; CI will apply in a canary VPC first.
4) Rollout: enable deny-by-default in a canary environment for non-customer-facing infra, observe for 48h, then incrementally roll across environments.
Risk mitigations: leave inbound SG rules untouched; NACLs are off by default; provide `egress_break_glass` list for emergency CIDR/port exceptions.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests: terratest in Go for CRUD of SGs/NACLs and private DNS.
- Security scans: tfsec + checkov, configured to fail CI on HIGH findings.
- Integration: terraform plan/apply in ephemeral AWS account via CI job `ci/module-perimeter-infra`.
- Observability: create a smoke check that queries Route53 private zone records and validates VPC association; CloudWatch metric emitted when deny-by-default is enabled and any flow logs show blocked outbound connections above threshold.
- Health checks: a lambda-based prober (deployed by module when `create_health_prober=true`) runs outbound probes to allowed destinations and reports to CloudWatch with a defined namespace `Redwood/Perimeter/Health`.
ci_and_release:
- Module lives in infra/modules/network-perimeter with semver tags (v1.0.0 initial).
- PR checklist: automated terratest run, tfsec/checkov report, README updated, changelog entry.
- Release flow: bump minor for non-breaking additions, major for behavioral default changes (eg: make deny-by-default true).
- Backwards compatibility policy included in README.
- Example consumer templates under `examples/` demonstrating import, mapping, and canary vars.
- Release artifact: registry-compatible zip + CHANGELOG.md

2026-02-25 Marina Ortega (security): Reviewed PR. Requested additional auditing tags and an allowlist for managed services IP ranges. Also requested documented justification for NACL usage. Added as follow-up task.

2026-03-01 Devon Patel (infra-qa): Terratest added. CI job `ci-module-perimeter` now runs plan for dev/staging. Found edge-case: AWS provider race when creating SG and associating to ENIs; added retry logic in module and test harness.

2026-03-05 Liam Chen: Addressed Marina's feedback; added `managed_service_prefixes` variable and `audit_reason` tag. Added import helper script `scripts/generate_imports.py`. Marking for security review and scheduling canary rollout in staging (2026-03-12).
